about: Locked files changed after the sealed run under protocol_lock.json (sha256 f6c1b3af..., tree 2ae513f) had finished on 2026-09-25. Each change is to reporting checks or tests; none touches a file the sealed commands executed differently, and every sealed output was written before these changes. tests/test_sealed_data.py accepts a changed locked file only with its exact current sha256 here. ADR 0010.

files.why: Check C looked for every sourced numbers.csv row under \devnum{}, so a sealed figure quoted in prose (a 'sealed.' key) always failed; it now looks under the key's own macro. run() gains sealed_prose so that a pass that reads no exact or online output can leave the sealed prose to the pass that reads them all.

The legacy paper-prints pass (outputs/paper_tables) reads no exact or online output; once the sealed exact run exists it leaves the sealed prose to check_exact_paper_prints, which checks it against every sealed output.

The refusal test asserted the pre-freeze reason ('no frozen protocol_lock.json'); after the freeze the same call is refused for lacking --unseal. It now asserts the requirement (refused, nothing written) in either state.

The lock check counted one ledger row per hashed input, which a second freeze breaks by writing the same rows again; it now requires a row for each input. After the freeze it accepts a changed locked file only when this declaration lists it with its current bytes.
Tests for the two check_paper_numbers changes: a sourced sealed figure in prose counts as printed under \sealednum{}, and a pass told to leave the sealed prose alone does not count an unknown figure.
